knowledge:
- key_parameters: PEmethod=Controls how plating efficiencies are processed; "fit" (default, fits PEs as intercepts/model parameters, statistically preferred) or "fix" (conventional normalization) ;; method=Estimation method; "ml" (default, Maximum-Likelihood using glm with Poisson family and log link) or "ls" (Least Squares using lm) ;; curvevar=Character string specifying the column name in the data frame that distinguishes different survival curves (e.g., "cline") ;; A=First treatment factor name in 2-way ANOVA (e.g., "siRNA") ;; B=Second treatment factor name in 2-way ANOVA (e.g., "x5fuCis") ;; param=Parametrisation option for 2-way ANOVA; "A/B" (default, nested version) or "A*B" (with interaction)
- alternatives: Maximum-Likelihood (ML) is preferred over Least Squares (LS) because ML parameter estimations for Poisson distributed data theoretically yield smaller variances.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing colony formation assay data to fit linear-quadratic radiation survival curves, compare survival curves between different cell lines/treatments, or perform 2-way ANOVA to test for treatment interactions (e.g., chemosensitisation).
- pitfalls: High dispersion parameters indicate poor fit or experimental anomalies. A dispersion cut-off of 9.0 is recommended for PEmethod="fit" (corresponding to 3 Poisson standard deviations), and 12.0 for PEmethod="fix". If exceeded, specific replicate experiments may need to be removed. Input data frames must contain exact column names: "Exp", "ncells", and "ncolonies", plus "dose" for survival curves.

workflows.name: lq_survival_curve_analysis
workflows.intent: Fit linear-quadratic cell survival curves to colony formation assay data, evaluate goodness-of-fit, and compare curves between different experimental groups.
input: cellsurv_data.txt (tab-delimited text file containing columns: cline, Exp, dose, ncells, ncolonies)
workflows.stages: 1. Load and inspect the data ;; 2. Fit the LQ model for a single cell line/group ;; 3. Print fit coefficients and calculate mean survival fractions ;; 4. Generate diagnostic plots for individual experiments ;; 5. Compare two survival curves statistically ;; 6. Plot the compared curves together
workflows.code:
library(CFAssay)
datatab <- read.table(system.file("doc", "expl1_cellsurvcurves.txt",
                                  package="CFAssay"), header=TRUE, sep="\t")
names(datatab)
head(datatab, 3)
X <- subset(datatab, cline=="okf6TERT1")
dim(X)
fit <- cellsurvLQfit(X)
print(fit)
plot(fit)
S0 <- pes(X)$S0
names(S0) <- pes(X)$Exp
sfpmean(X, S0)
plotExp(fit)
fitcomp <- cellsurvLQdiff(datatab, curvevar="cline")
print(fitcomp)
plot(cellsurvLQfit(subset(datatab, cline=="okf6TERT1")), col=1)
plot(cellsurvLQfit(subset(datatab, cline=="cal33")), col=2, add=TRUE)
legend(0, 0.02, c("OKF6/TERT1", "CAL 33"), text.col=1:2)

workflows.name: two_way_anova_cfa
workflows.intent: Perform a two-way ANOVA with interaction on colony formation assay data to test for synergistic or sensitizing effects between two treatment factors.
input: anova_data.txt (tab-delimited text file containing columns: Exp, siRNA, x5fuCis, ncells, ncolonies)
workflows.stages: 1. Load and inspect the two-way experimental data ;; 2. Fit the two-way ANOVA model with interaction ;; 3. Print detailed ANOVA results and effect sizes ;; 4. Generate diagnostic plots for the experiments
workflows.code:
library(CFAssay)
datatab <- read.table(system.file("doc", "exp2_2waycfa.txt", package="CFAssay"),
                      header=TRUE, sep="\t")
names(datatab)
head(datatab, 3)
fitcomp <- cfa2way(datatab, A="siRNA", B="x5fuCis", param="A/B")
print(fitcomp, labels=c(A="siRNA", B="x5fuCis"))
plotExp(fitcomp, labels=c(A="siRNA", B="x5fuCis"))
